appraisal_events.evidence: la génération de nobles qui a plus ou moins passé par Monseigneur Dupanloup parle un si mauvais français ... que le duc exprima ainsi sa pensée : « Il vaut mieux ne pas être couvert avant d'aller dehors, du moins en thèse générale. »
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator ironically singles out the duke's stilted, ungrammatical phrasing as an example of a supposedly refined class speaking poor French, mildly undercutting his aristocratic polish.

appraisal_events.evidence: Mme de Gallardon était en effet comme ces amoureux dédaignés qui veulent à toute force faire croire qu'ils sont plus aimés que ceux que choie leur belle.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator compares Gallardon to a spurned lover who insists, against the evidence, on being especially loved, exposing her praise of the duchess as self-deceiving envy rather than genuine intimacy.

status_effects.explanation: His affectedly formal but grammatically awkward remark is gently mocked, slightly deflating his aristocratic pretension to refinement.
Her insistence on the duchess's affection is framed by the narrator as self-deluding, reinforcing her position as an envious, largely spurned relation.
